summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance. In Alabama the age of majority is 19 (Ala. Code § 26-1-1), and for child abuse and neglect reporting a "child" is a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services (Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3)).

key_cases.case_name: Randolph County Department of Human Resources v. A.H.
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the juvenile court's judgment denying DHR's dependency petition and returning the child to his parents, holding that DHR's abandonment theory was unpreserved and that it had not challenged the finding that the mother could provide the necessary care.
key_cases.relevance: This is a published Alabama example of dismissal of a dependency petition and return of the child to the parents.
key_cases.quote: This court cannot consider an issue raised for the first time on appeal

key_cases.holding: On rehearing the Court held that the trial court erred in terminating the father's parental rights because the evidence did not prove any applicable statutory ground, refused to terminate his rights, and remanded for a custody determination rather than ordering immediate transfer of the child.
key_cases.relevance: When the statutory criteria are not proved, the correct outcome is refusal to terminate and a remand on custody, not a compromise judgment.
key_cases.quote: the evidence in this case does not tend to prove any of Alabama's applicable statutory criteria for terminating the father's parental rights

key_cases.case_name: P.S. v. Jefferson County Department of Human Resources
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a termination judgment because DHR never identified the mother's parenting defect, never communicated what she needed to change, and was relieved of reasonable efforts when the child was five months old, so no clear and convincing evidence satisfied Ala. Code 12-15-319(a).
key_cases.relevance: Reversal and remand, not termination, is the outcome when DHR fails to meet 12-15-319(a).
key_cases.quote: DHR did not provide the mother the opportunity to correct any conduct or condition that might have been a barrier to reunification with the child

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed and held that a parent, who has a right to appointed counsel in a termination case, may raise a claim of ineffective assistance of that counsel by a Rule 60(b)(6) motion filed within a reasonable time, and that a motion filed within sixty days after the Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the termination was timely.
key_cases.relevance: It identifies the Rule 60(b)(6) motion as the means of reopening a closed termination case when the ordinary fourteen-day postjudgment window was practically unusable.
key_cases.quote: In a parental-rights-termination case, a parent has a right to appointed counsel.
